research_rationale: EO 26 (1887-08-25) directs Treasury to instruct customs collectors to admit qualifying foreign soldier guests of the Chicago October 1887 encampment with baggage, uniforms, arms and equipment free of customs duties, retaining formalities necessary to ensure reexportation. The event reference bounds eligible guests but supplies no express calendar sunset or proof of actual performance. No first cessation of the instruction/admission command or discharge of reexportation conditions is established. Held OCR is severely corrupt; required visual inspection could not be performed with available renderer. EO 11285 operative sections 1-6 concern interest equalization tax and supersede EO 11224, not this order. No complete whole-case claim is submitted.
savings_reason: Reexportation formalities expressly qualify duty-free admission; whether admitted articles were reexported, conditions discharged, or accrued customs consequences remained is unproved. No absence of residuals inferred.
